content:
Still Bas Braams from CWI, Amsterdam [0]. My current Lean effort is implementation of B. C. Carlson’s approach to the special functions of mathematical physics [1] and related higher-dimensional special functions. This approach involves integration of functions over the multivariate standard simplex relative to a complex Dirichlet measure, or a complex Dirichlet density times coordinate Lebesgue measure. The basic elements of this could be of broader use. They have actually grown further than I had expected in my earlier postings on the subject [2], [3].
With one or more Mathlib PR in mind I would much appreciate feedback on the structure and content of any of the following elements. They are five *.lean files in my Github space [4] in the StdSimplexMeasure folder under lean-projects [5].
The outer design is mine, but in the development I relied extensively on LLM and all the proofs were supplied by LLM (primarily ChatGPT 5.6). The contents of PositiveSimplex.lean should be revisited if and when PR #37910 [6] becomes a part of Mathlib; there is overlap.
The five files are the following.

Coordinates.lean

This file develops algebraic and ordered coordinate constructions for stdSimplex R ι. The affine coordinate chart is available over a commutative ring, while statements involving simplex inequalities use a compatible partial order. The final section gives the topological properties of these coordinate charts over ℝ.

PositiveSimplex.lean

This file evaluates the Lebesgue volume of the set of nonnegative coordinate vectors whose coordinate sum is bounded by a nonnegative real number. The proof first treats coordinates indexed by Fin n, by induction and slicing, and then transports the result to any finite type.

Measure.lean

This file defines the coordinate-normalized measure on the affine hull of the real standard simplex. It proves independence of the omitted coordinate, permutation invariance, the simplex-volume formula, boundary-nullity, and the push-forward formula for coordinate aggregation. This coordinate measure differs by a dimension-dependent constant from the Euclidean Hausdorff measure on the affine hull.

Integral.lean

This file develops change-of-coordinates, slicing, permutation, monomial, and aggregation formulas for integrals with respect to stdSimplexMeasure.

Dirichlet.lean

The multivariate Dirichlet measure [7, Ch 49] is defined on the standard simplex in symmetric variables, i.e. stdSimplex ℝ ι, or Ek-1 embedded in ℝk where k = card ι.

References
